description: Rotterdam 3D is the City of Rotterdam's public 3D viewer, built on VC Map, whose configuration lists the layers it serves. Coverage: the municipality of Rotterdam. The 3D content includes LOD2 buildings with and without textures, planned buildings, bridges (model and textured), storage tanks and moorings at LOD2, a 3D version of the Dutch large-scale topography (BGT), a photorealistic mesh in five city sections, terrain models (current and 2024), point clouds of dormers and vegetation, trees above and below ground (root zones), street furniture such as lamp posts, benches, bins, bike lockers, parking meters and EV charging points, and a public layer of underground cables and pipes (LVZK). A further group of about 70 map layers from the city's ArcGIS services covers public space assets such as electrical cabinets, distribution cabinets, gullies, culverts, civil engineering structures (kunstwerken), traffic detectors, road markings and road sections, quay walls and embankments, harbour basins, watercourses, guard rails, traffic signs and temporary traffic measures, with national cadastral and BAG building layers from PDOK. Format and access: a web viewer with 3D Tiles (Cesium tilesets), terrain and WMS layers from public endpoints; free to view. Licence: not stated in the configuration; terms were not read. Caveats: the viewer is script-driven, so layer metadata, update dates and download options were not read; the underground utility layer is marked public but its completeness is unknown. Simulation uses: a detailed city digital twin of buildings, bridges, utilities and street assets for flood, heat and emergency response studies and asset management. Related records: 3DBAG (data-3dbag) is the national LOD2 building model of the Netherlands.
